Word detective: follow the clues

Flour or flower? A word with two opposite meanings? Follow three short lessons, try the clues yourself and find the link in a word puzzle.

Start learning →

By Biel Sardà · Published 4 Oct 2026 · Suggest a correction

From the basics · 3 lessons · No timer

What you’ll explore

A flower belongs in a vase. Flour belongs in a cake. They sound alike, so how do you know which one someone means?

Start with that little mix-up, discover words that can pull in opposite directions, then use the same detective habit in a Connections puzzle. Read a little, try an example and check what you have learned. There is no timer.

A few words worth knowing

Context
The words and situation around a clue that help you understand it.
Homophones
Words that share a pronunciation but have different meanings.
Contronym
A word with meanings that can be opposites.
